The author names three different ways in which a man may react to sudden danger. What are they?

options.a: He may be paralysed with fear, seized with panic or act like an inferior animal.
options.b: He may be paralysed with fear, run away or fight.
options.c: He may flee in panic, or fight back or stand still.
options.d: He may be paralysed with fear or seized with panic, or as if by miracle become possessed of the necessary courage, and face the danger.

faqs.a: He may be paralysed with fear or seized with panic, or as if by miracle become possessed of the necessary courage, and face the danger.
faqs.e: When we are suddenly confronted with any terrible danger, the change of nature we undergo is equally great. In some cases fear paralyses us. Like animals we stand still, powerless to move a step in fright, or to lift a hand in defence of our lives, and sometimes we are seized with panic, and again, act more like the inferior animals than rational beings. On the other hand, frequently in cases of sudden extreme peril, which cannot be escaped by flight, and must be instantly faced, even the most timid men at once, as if by miracle, become possessed of the necessary courage, sharp quick apprehension, and swift decision. This is a miracle very common in nature. Man and the inferior animals alike, when confronted with almost certain death 'gather resolution from despair', but there can really be no trace of so debilitating a feeling in the person fighting, or prepared to fight, for dear life. At such times the mind is clearer than it has ever been; the nerves are steel; there is nothing felt but a wonderful strength and fury and daring. Looking back at certain perilous moments in my own life, I remember them with a kind of joy; not that there was any joyful excitement then, but because they brought me a new experience—a new nature, as it were—and lifted me for a time above myself.

faqs.q: The rational number with recurring decimal expansion 0.1̅2̅ is
faqs.e:
A repeating decimal 0.overline(12) can be written as a fraction with the repeating block over as many 9s as digits in the block, so 0.121212... = 12/99, which simplifies to 4/33.

Checking 4/33 by division confirms it repeats as 0.1212..., matching the given decimal.

faqs.q: The average of four consecutive numbers A, B, C and D is 35.5. Then, the product of B and C is
faqs.e:
Four consecutive numbers averaging 35.5 must be 34, 35, 36, 37, since their sum is 4 × 35.5 = 142 and consecutive integers centred there are 34-37.

B and C are the two middle numbers, 35 and 36, so their product is 35 × 36 = 1260.

faqs.q: The smallest positive number which is exactly divisible by 450, 600 and 900 is
faqs.e:
Finding the LCM: 450 = 2×3²×5², 600 = 2³×3×5², 900 = 2²×3²×5². Taking the highest powers gives 2³×3²×5².

That works out to 8 × 9 × 25 = 1800, the smallest number divisible by all three.

faqs.q: Two numbers x and y are such that x : y = 2 : 3 and their highest common factor is 900. Then xy =
faqs.e:
Since x and y are in ratio 2:3 with 2 and 3 sharing no common factor, HCF 900 is the multiplier, so the numbers are 1800 and 2700.

The least common multiple equals the product of the ratio parts times the HCF, 2 × 3 × 900 = 5400.

faqs.q: Rs. 8750/- is to be distributed to three persons P, Q and R. Q receives 1/4 of what P and R receive together and P receives 2/5 of what Q and R receive together. Then, P receives the amount (in rupees)
faqs.e:
Since Q gets 1/4 of (P+R), Q equals one-fifth of the total, so Q = 8750/5 = 1750.

Since P gets 2/5 of (Q+R), P equals two-sevenths of the total, so P = (2/7) × 8750 = 2500.

faqs.q: Two numbers are in the ratio 5 : 7. If 8 is subtracted from each number, then the ratio becomes 2 : 3. The product of the numbers is
faqs.e:
Let the numbers be 5k and 7k. After subtracting 8 from each, (5k-8):(7k-8) = 2:3, which gives 3(5k-8) = 2(7k-8), so 15k-24 = 14k-16, hence k = 8.

The numbers are 40 and 56, so their product is 40 × 56 = 2240.

faqs.q: The length of a rectangle is decreased by 10% but the area remains the same. Then, percentage increase in the breadth of the rectangle is
faqs.e:
If length becomes 0.9 of original, breadth must become 1/0.9 = 10/9 of original to keep area constant.

That is an increase of 1/9, which as a percentage is 11 1/9%.

faqs.q: The population of a small village increases by 8% annually. If its present population is 23328, then the population 2 years ago was
faqs.e:
Working backward twice by dividing by 1.08 each year: 23328 / 1.08 = 21600, then 21600 / 1.08 = 20000.

So the population 2 years ago was 20000.

faqs.q: A and B started a business investing Rs. 3.5 lakhs and 6.5 lakhs respectively. After six months, A left the business and C joined B with an investment of Rs. 7.5 lakhs. The share of C (in lakhs of rupees) in the year-end profit of Rs. 2.4 lakhs is
faqs.e:
A's capital-months are 3.5×6 = 21, B's are 6.5×12 = 78, and C's are 7.5×6 = 45, giving a total of 144 capital-month units.

C's share of the ratio is 45/144, so C receives (45/144) × 2.4 = 0.75 lakh.

faqs.q: Three individuals A, B, C start a company and contribute a total of Rs. 5,20,000/-. A contributes Rs. 40,000/- more than B and B contributes Rs. 60,000/- more than C. If the company earns a profit of Rs. 1,95,000/-, the share of C is (in rupees)
faqs.e:
Let C's contribution be x, so B = x+60,000 and A = x+100,000. Their sum is 3x+160,000 = 520,000, giving x = 120,000.

C's share of the profit is (120,000/520,000) × 195,000 = 45,000.

faqs.q: The sum of K numbers is 2000 and their average is 50. If 91 is included into the list, then the new average is
faqs.e:
Since the average of K numbers is 50 and their sum is 2000, K must be 40.

Adding 91 gives a new sum of 2091 over 41 numbers, so the new average is 2091/41 = 51.

faqs.q: The average age of a family of 3 members was 29 years six years ago. After that a child was born. Today, the average age of the family is 25 years. The present age of the child is
faqs.e:
Six years ago the total age of the three members was 3×29 = 87, and today's family total is 4×25 = 100.

Had the child not existed, natural ageing alone would have raised the three members' total by 3×6 = 18, to 105; since the actual total rose only to 100, the shortfall of 5 gives the child's present age as 5.

faqs.q: The cost price of a TV set for a shopkeeper is Rs. 22,000/-. The shopkeeper increased its price by 15%. Then he sold the TV set at a discount of 20%. The actual loss for the shopkeeper in percentage is
faqs.e:
After a 15% mark-up the marked price is 22000 × 1.15 = 25300, and a 20% discount brings the selling price to 25300 × 0.8 = 20240.

The loss is 22000-20240 = 1760, which as a percentage of the cost price is 1760/22000 = 8%.

faqs.q: A shopkeeper sold a mobile at a profit of 8% to a second shopkeeper. The second shopkeeper sold it to a third shopkeeper at a profit of 6%. If the third shopkeeper paid Rs. 2862/-, the cost price of the mobile for the first shopkeeper is (in rupees)
faqs.e:
Working backward, the second shopkeeper's selling price satisfies 1.06x = 2862, so x = 2700.

The first shopkeeper's cost then satisfies 1.08y = 2700, giving y = 2500.

faqs.q: A sum of Rs. 12,000/- given at simple interest rate of 12% per annum becomes Rs. 16,320/- in T years. The value of T is (in years)
faqs.e:
The interest earned is 16320-12000 = 4320, and simple interest per year is 12000 × 0.12 = 1440.

So T = 4320/1440 = 3 years.

faqs.q: The difference between compound interest and simple interest on an amount of Rs. A at 8% per annum for 2 years is Rs. 800/-. Then, the amount A is (in rupees)
faqs.e:
For 2 years, the difference between CI and SI equals A × (rate)², here A × 0.08² = A × 0.0064.

Setting A × 0.0064 = 800 gives A = 1,25,000.

faqs.q: Mohan can repair an Instrument in 40 hours. Ram can repair the same instrument in 30 hours. Mohan and Ram work together to repair the same instrument for 8 hours. Then, Mohan goes away. The number of hours that Ram takes to complete the work is (in hours)
faqs.e:
Together they complete (1/40+1/30) = 7/120 of the work per hour, so in 8 hours they finish 56/120 = 7/15 of the job.

The remaining 8/15 of the work is done by Ram alone at 1/30 per hour, taking (8/15)×30 = 16 hours.

faqs.q: A person A can do a work in 20 days. He works for 5 days and stops doing the work. Then, a second person B completes the remaining work in 9 days. If A and B work together, how long will they take to complete the work?
faqs.e:
A does 5/20 = 1/4 of the work in 5 days, leaving 3/4 for B to finish in 9 days, so B's rate is (3/4)/9 = 1/12 per day.

Together A and B do 1/20+1/12 = 8/60 = 2/15 per day, so they finish in 15/2 = 7 1/2 days.

faqs.q: A train 80 meters long is running at 108 km/hr. The time that the train will take to pass a platform of 130 meters long is (in seconds)
faqs.e:
108 km/hr converts to 30 m/s, and the train must cover its own length plus the platform, 80+130 = 210 metres.

Time = 210/30 = 7 seconds.

faqs.q: Two trains of lengths 100 meters and 80 meters are moving in the same direction at speeds of 80 km/hr. and 60 km/hr. respectively. The time taken by the first train to cross the second train is (in seconds)
faqs.e:
The relative speed is 80-60 = 20 km/hr, which converts to 50/9 m/s, and the combined length to be covered is 100+80 = 180 metres.

Time = 180 / (50/9) = 32.4 seconds.

faqs.q: A committee of 6 members is to be formed out of 6 men and 3 women. The number of committees that can be formed in which at least one woman is included is
faqs.e:
The total ways to pick any 6 from 9 people is C(9,6) = 84, and the all-men committee (choosing all 6 from the 6 men) is only 1 way.

Subtracting that single no-women case gives 84-1 = 83 committees with at least one woman.

faqs.q:
The ratios of surface areas of 2 cubes are given in List I. In List II, the ratios of their volumes are given. Match them:

List–I
(a) 1 : 16
(b) 1 : 25
(c) 1 : 9

List–II
(i) 1 : 125
(ii) 1 : 27
(iii) 1 : 36
(iv) 1 : 64
faqs.e:
For similar solids, if surface areas are in ratio 1:16, the linear scale ratio is 1:4 (square root), so volumes are in ratio 1:4³ = 1:64, matching (a)-(iv).

For 1:25 the linear ratio is 1:5, giving volumes 1:125, matching (b)-(i); for 1:9 the linear ratio is 1:3, giving volumes 1:27, matching (c)-(ii).

If WALK, TRIM and MAY are coded as 8243, 6517 and 729, then RAILWAY is coded as:
faqs.e:
Each letter maps to a fixed digit from the given codes: W=8,A=2,L=4,K=3,T=6,R=5,I=1,M=7,Y=9. RAILWAY uses R-A-I-L-W-A-Y, giving digits 5-2-1-4-8-2-9.

Putting these together gives the code 5214829.

faqs.q: If SURESH is coded as TWSGTJ then PRINCE is coded as:
faqs.e:

Applying the same positional shifts to PRINCE gives Q, T, J, P, D, G, i.e. QTJPDG.

faqs.q: If GNBJDX is the code for HOCKEY, then the word coded as BQHBJDS is:
faqs.e:

Decoding BQHBJDS by shifting each letter forward by one gives CRICKET.

faqs.q: In a code POLICE is coded as SROLFH. The code word for STATION in that code is:

Applying the same +3 shift to STATION gives VWDWLRQ.

faqs.q: If 1st February in a non-leap year is a Sunday, then 31st May is a
faqs.e:
From 1st February to 31st May spans 28 (Feb, non-leap) + 31 (Mar) + 30 (Apr) + 30 days into May = 119 days after 1st February.

119 days is exactly 17 weeks, so 31st May falls on the same day as 1st February, a Sunday.

faqs.q: If 26th January of a leap year is a Sunday then 15th August of that year will be a
faqs.e:
From 26th January to 15th August in a leap year spans 5(Jan)+29(Feb)+31(Mar)+30(Apr)+31(May)+30(Jun)+31(Jul)+15(Aug) = 202 days.

202 days is 28 weeks plus 6 days, so counting 6 days forward from Sunday lands on Saturday.

faqs.q: A meeting of a committee is being held. One member reached the venue 20 minutes before 9.35 A.M. Second member came half an hour later than the first member. The second member was late by 40 minutes. The scheduled time of the meeting was
faqs.e:
The first member arrived at 9.35 minus 20 minutes, which is 9.15 A.M., and the second member arrived half an hour after that, at 9.45 A.M.

Since the second member was 40 minutes late, the scheduled time was 9.45 minus 40 minutes, which is 9.05 A.M.

faqs.e:

Only when all three pairwise combined rates (I), (II) and (III) are known can the three individual rates be solved for and then combined, so all three statements together are needed.

faqs.e:

faqs.q: The diameters of two concentric circles are 10 cm and 16 cm respectively. The area of the region between the circles is (in square cm)
faqs.e:
The radii are 5 cm and 8 cm, so the area between the circles is π(8²-5²) = π(64-25).

That works out to 39π square cm.

faqs.e:

Here that is 20²/100 = 4%, so there is an overall loss of 4%.
